input: text is an ASCII string of length n <= 10000000; k is an integer in [0, 10000000]. Empty text and k > n are allowed. Python integers exclude bool; standard containers/built-ins only. Preconditions are declared, not checked. Size bounds do not promise runtime feasibility.
return: Count length-k contiguous substrings with k distinct characters; return zero when no complete window exists. For k=0 there are n+1 empty windows, including one on empty text.
mutation_aliasing: No caller-owned input is mutated. No state survives on the Solution instance. Scalar/string results have value semantics; private work containers do not escape.
numeric: Counts and indices are at most n; the zero-width result is n+1, still exactly representable.
complexity: O(n) expected time using ordinary hash maps, O(min(n,k,128)) auxiliary space. Each character enters and leaves the sliding window at most once.
source_accounting: The full standalone source is 640 UTF-8 bytes, including class/method wrappers, built-ins, allocations, whitespace and terminal newline. No hidden helper or source expansion. Any frozen solve-entry adapter must be stored and charged additionally.
